newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels said seeking third party mediation.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels said seeking third party mediation.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger rebels have called for third party mediation to help end the country's ethnic conflict, a newspaper reported on Sunday.

The independent Sunday Times quoted Shanker Master, a rebel leader in the Indian Ocean island, as saying they wanted third party mediation because the Tamil people had been betrayed by successive governments and had no confidence in direct talks.
The government has declined previous offers of third party mediation to end the war, saying it was an internal matter.
"We'd like to find a lasting solution through dialogue," the newspaper quoted Shanker Master as saying. "If this is not possible we will be compelled to continue our armed struggle."

The Sunday Times also said Shanker Master demanded that the army withdraw to positions held before it captured the northern rebel stronghold of Jaffna and that it recognise Tiger rebels as the sole representative of minority Tamils.

The government has rejected both conditions in the past and insisted the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels lay down their weapons before talks and also agree to a specific time frame for negotiations.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government this week released sections of a draft constitution which in its full form would offer wide autonomy to Sri Lanka's minorities and aims to end the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
LTTE rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for Tamils in the north and east of the island. The country's majority people are Sinhalese.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, but the rebels say the death toll is higher.
